metrics.label: Heart rate
howToMeasure: Sit quietly for 5 minutes first.
Wear the watch snugly above the wrist bone, or use a pulse oximeter on a warm finger.
Stay still and silent while it reads.
Record the value and whether you were resting or had just exercised.
metrics.whyItMatters: Heart rate responds to fluid shifts, fitness changes, stress, illness and sleep loss.
metrics.frequencyHint: Continuous from a wearable, or a spot check after exercise.

metrics.label: Resting heart rate
howToMeasure: Measure soon after waking, before caffeine or exercise.
Lie or sit still for 5 minutes.
Count for 60 seconds or let the device read for a full minute.
Measure at the same time each day.
metrics.whyItMatters: A sustained rise above your own normal can reflect poor recovery, stress, dehydration or illness.

metrics.label: Heart-rate variability
howToMeasure: Best measured overnight by a wearable.
For a spot reading, sit still and breathe normally for 2 minutes.
Compare only readings of the same type (SDNN or RMSSD).
metrics.whyItMatters: Falling HRV relative to your normal often accompanies stress, fatigue and poor recovery.

metrics.label: Systolic BP
howToMeasure: Sit upright, back supported, feet flat, for 5 minutes before measuring.
Place the cuff on the bare upper arm at heart level.
Stay still and quiet during the measurement.
Take two readings one minute apart and record both.
metrics.whyItMatters: Fluid shifts and cardiovascular deconditioning change blood pressure in spaceflight.

metrics.label: Diastolic BP
howToMeasure: Entered together with systolic pressure from the same cuff reading.
metrics.whyItMatters: Read together with systolic pressure.

metrics.label: Blood glucose
howToMeasure: Wash and dry your hands first.
Use a fresh test strip and lancet.
Note whether you are fasting or how long since your last meal.
Record the value straight away.
metrics.whyItMatters: Diet, activity, stress and illness all affect glucose; nutrition is hard to keep ideal far from Earth.

metrics.label: Body temperature
howToMeasure: Wait 15 minutes after eating, drinking or exercise.
Use the same thermometer and site (ear, mouth or forehead) every time.
Follow the thermometer's own instructions for placement.
Record the site you used in the note.
metrics.whyItMatters: Fever can be an early sign of infection; immune function changes in spaceflight.
metrics.frequencyHint: Weekly, and whenever you feel unwell.

metrics.label: Sleeping wrist temperature
howToMeasure: Measured automatically overnight by a compatible watch.
Only changes relative to your own normal are meaningful; it is not comparable with oral temperature.
metrics.whyItMatters: Shifts from your nightly norm can accompany illness, stress or sleep disruption.

metrics.label: Blood oxygen
howToMeasure: Warm your hands; cold fingers give low readings.
Sit still and rest your hand on a surface at heart level.
Wait until the reading is stable (about 30 seconds).
If it is unexpectedly low, re-measure on another finger.
metrics.whyItMatters: Oxygen saturation reflects lung function and cabin atmosphere.

metrics.label: Respiratory rate
howToMeasure: Rest quietly for 5 minutes.
Count breaths for a full 60 seconds without changing how you breathe.
Wearables estimate this during sleep.
metrics.whyItMatters: Changes can reflect illness, cabin air quality or stress.
metrics.frequencyHint: Nightly from a wearable or weekly spot check.

metrics.label: Sleep per night
howToMeasure: Count time actually asleep, not time in bed.
A wearable records this automatically.
For manual entry, estimate when you fell asleep and woke up.
metrics.whyItMatters: Light-dark cycles, noise, workload and confinement disrupt sleep in space.

metrics.label: Sleep quality
howToMeasure: Rate how rested you feel on waking: 1 = very poor, 5 = excellent.
metrics.whyItMatters: How rested you feel complements measured sleep time.

metrics.label: Mood
howToMeasure: Pick the face that best matches how you feel overall today.
There is no right answer; honesty keeps your baseline useful.
metrics.whyItMatters: Isolation, confinement and distance from home affect behavioural health.

metrics.label: Stress
howToMeasure: Rate today's stress: 1 = very calm, 5 = extremely stressed.
metrics.whyItMatters: Sustained stress affects sleep, mood, immunity and performance.

metrics.label: Workload
howToMeasure: Rate today's workload: 1 = very light, 5 = overwhelming.
metrics.whyItMatters: High workload combined with poor sleep is a common strain pattern.

metrics.label: Appetite
howToMeasure: Rate today's appetite: 1 = no appetite, 5 = normal or good.
metrics.whyItMatters: Reduced intake is common in spaceflight and contributes to mass loss.

metrics.label: Fluid intake
howToMeasure: Log each drink as you have it, or estimate the day's total in the evening.
metrics.whyItMatters: Fluid intake affects heart rate, blood pressure and wellbeing.

metrics.label: Exercise minutes
howToMeasure: Count minutes of planned countermeasure exercise (resistance and aerobic).
A watch records this automatically.
metrics.whyItMatters: Exercise is the main countermeasure against bone, muscle and cardiovascular deconditioning.

metrics.label: Steps / activity
howToMeasure: Counted automatically by your phone or watch.
metrics.whyItMatters: A drop in general activity can signal fatigue or low mood.

metrics.label: Body mass
howToMeasure: Weigh at the same time of day, ideally on waking after using the toilet.
Wear similar clothing each time.
In microgravity, use the mass-measurement device per procedure.
metrics.whyItMatters: Mass loss can reflect low intake or muscle loss.

metrics.label: Radiation dose rate
howToMeasure: Keep the detector in the same place relative to your body.
Let it run continuously; do not shield or move it during readings.
metrics.whyItMatters: Dose rate shows the current radiation environment.

metrics.label: Cumulative dose
howToMeasure: Calculated by the app from the dose rate; a device counter is also recorded if available.
metrics.whyItMatters: Cumulative dose is tracked against the mission dose budget.

metrics.label: Count rate
howToMeasure: Recorded from the detector's counter.
metrics.whyItMatters: Raw detector counts; converted to dose only with a configured, labelled calibration.

metrics.label: Cabin CO₂
howToMeasure: Read the cabin sensor at head height in your work area.
metrics.whyItMatters: Elevated CO₂ in closed habitats is linked to headaches and reduced performance.

metrics.label: Cabin temperature
howToMeasure: Read the cabin sensor in your sleep or work area.
metrics.whyItMatters: Thermal comfort affects sleep and performance.

metrics.label: Symptom report
howToMeasure: Pick the symptom, rate severity 1 (mild) to 3 (severe), and note when it started.
metrics.whyItMatters: Symptoms are often the earliest sign that something needs attention.
metrics.frequencyHint: Whenever you notice one, and at daily check-in.
